title: The Year One unsealing reading
statement: The Dead Sea Scrolls came to light in the winter of 1946/47 — the first year of the era the canon counts from the 1945/1946 threshold — and the corpus reads the timing as an instance of the Apocalypse-as-unveiling: the oldest biblical manuscripts surfacing in the opening year of the period the canon designates for the uncovering of what was concealed; the reading is synthesis on a coincidence of dates, labelled speculative, with the discovery history itself carried at documentary strength.

includes: The documentary layer at full strength: the discovery chronology (winter 1946/47), the acquisition and authentication history the Explainer narrates, and the scholarly dating of the manuscripts
The calendrical fact: the canon's era opens at the 1945/1946 threshold, so the discovery falls in its first year
The unveiling reading, labelled speculative: the timing read as an instance of the Apocalypse-as-unveiling recorded in woh-claim-0015 — a meaningful surfacing, not an asserted intervention
excludes: Any causal or intervention claim about the discovery; the record reads a timing, and says so
Extension to other discoveries by date-matching; each candidate instance would need its own record
The Scrolls' content readings, which belong to the corpus's textual work, not to this timing claim
Probability arguments; the corpus does not model the coincidence

source_references.locator: TBWTT-1:47 (chosen after the first atomic explosion of 1945); TBWTT-5:1 ('1946, year 1 of the new era'); TBWTT-5:7 (the Fish Gate / Aquarius material)
The standard account of the discovery, acquisition, and dating

alternatives.statement: A century of Near Eastern archaeology produces discoveries every year; selecting the one that lands on the era's first year is textbook selection effect.
The era's threshold was announced decades after the discovery; the alignment is constructed backwards and could not have failed.
The discovery's own dating (late 1946 versus early 1947, and the era's 1945/1946/1950 boundary questions) gives the alignment more play than the reading admits.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0015 is revised or retired.
Documentary revision of the discovery chronology changes the calendrical fact.
Public prose begins asserting intervention or extending the pattern by date-matching, which this record excludes.
The boundary-reconciliation underlying the era's opening (recorded in the 0003 apparatus) is revised.
